subject: Urgent: inference latency spike & reserved throughput shortfall
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@ethershift.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@ethershift.com
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: inference latency spike & reserved throughput shortfall

Naomi / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp degradation this morning across our production inference endpoints (model: quantify-gpt-13b). Key observations from 02:00–08:30 PDT: 
- 99th latency jumped from ~230ms to ~1.8s, p95 from 260ms to 540ms.
- 5xx error rate increased to ~3.6% (previous baseline <0.1%).
- Our reserved throughput (contracted 6,500 QPS) is being throttled — sustained observed serving throughput is ~2,400 QPS for the last 4 hours despite traffic at expected levels.

This is impacting critical user flows. We've already routed lower-priority traffic to a fallback region but need Redwood to triage immediately. Attached is a short CSV snapshot of the request log and sample traces (ethershift-metrics-9-03.csv).

Can we schedule a bridge in the next 30 minutes? We need either a mitigation (fallback model, temporary burst) or a clear rollback path. Please escalate to engineering and ops.

— Maria Gomez
Head of Platform, Ethershift

(attachment: ethershift-metrics-9-03.csv)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@ethershift.com>
Cc: support@ethershift.com, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: inference latency spike & reserved throughput shortfall

Maria — thanks for the clear signal and the CSV. We’re on it.

Immediate asks so we can triage in parallel:
- confirm model version (you listed quantify-gpt-13b; is this v1.4 or v1.3?)
- last deploy time and any new prompt patterns (longer system prompts?)
- whether you’ve recently increased max_seq_length or changed client-side batching

Short-term mitigations we can apply now (pending your GO):
1) Enable prefix/KV cache pinning for hot routes (reduces KV cache evictions).
2) Route a fraction (10–20%) to the v1.3 variant if available; we can pin until root cause found.
3) Authorize a temporary burst (2x reserved capacity) for 2 hours while we stabilize — I’ll request approval from our capacity team internally.

Proposed bridge: 10:00 PDT today. If that works, please share any extra traces and the model id. I’ll loop in Jonas and Irene for kernel/runtime analysis and Marcus on the customer commercial path.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference, inc.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: inference latency spike & reserved throughput shortfall

Naomi / team — quick read from the initial logs Naomi pulled in: 
- KV cache churn is very high for the quantify-gpt-13b endpoints — eviction rate spiked at 03:15 PDT, correlates with the first latency bump. Likely caused by a sudden increase in unique long prompts (many >1,200 tokens) which defeats prefix caching and forces full attention passes.
- We also see a change in kernel selection behaviour for this model family after the v1.4 rollout: on longer sequences the runtime shifts to a memory-friendlier kernel that has higher per-token latency. That explains p95/p99 jump even though p50 is near baseline.
- The reserved slot allocator is enforcing QPS ceilings correctly; the observed 2,400 QPS is what the farm can sustain given current memory/KV-cache pressure.

Short-term plan (recommend):
A) Roll traffic on the hot endpoints back to v1.3 (immediate rollback) — v1.3 uses a different kernel path and historically stays under burst headroom for similar sequences.
B) Immediately enable aggressive prefix caching for the top 20 routes and increase per-model KV cache allowance for Ethershift (config change).
C) Temporary burst request: +2x on reserved throughput for 2 hours while we complete A/B validation — this requires approval from capacity/finance.
D) Tune batching: lower max_batch_delay to reduce tail latency at peak — trades a small throughput delta for latency stability.

If we get GO on (A) + (C) we can stabilize within ~30–45 minutes. I’ll prepare the rollback job and a short validation runbook. Linking the runbook here: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/triage-gpu-saturation

— Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: SUMMARY & ACTIONS — Ethershift production stabilization (follow-up)

Team / Maria — quick summary of what we executed and next steps.

What we observed: sustained 5xx and tail latency increase on quantify-gpt-13b after v1.4 roll; KV cache eviction and kernel path change caused effective headroom collapse and reduced sustainable throughput to ~2.4k QPS.

What we did (timeline):
- 09:50 PDT (Sept 3): Jonas started rollback job and A/B validation on sample routes.
- 10:12 PDT: Rolled traffic to v1.3 for hot endpoints — immediate p95 improvement observed (p95 down from ~540ms to ~320ms in sample window).
- 10:25 PDT: Enabled expanded KV cache allowance and aggressive prefix caching for top 20 routes.
- 10:40 PDT: Authorized temporary burst (2x reserved throughput) while the rollback completed and we validated (approved internally).
- 11:05 PDT: Stabilized production; 5xx rate fell from 3.6% to 0.15% over 30 minutes. Sustained throughput climbing back toward contractual levels as KV pressure dropped.

Open / next steps:
- Engineering (Jonas/Irene): Long-term fix to ensure v1.4 kernel path selects lower-latency implementation for long sequences (action: root-cause PR and benchmark by 9/10).
- Product & Sales (Marcus/Naomi): Commercial remediation — Marcus recommends a 25% invoice credit for Sept platform usage while we complete the kernel/backport work.
- Ops: Add a preflight check for large-sequence deploys that simulates KV cache pressure (action: runbook update).

Attachments: redwood-triage-runbook.pdf (triage steps + rollback checklist), ethershift-metrics-9-03.csv (customer traces).

Maria — appreciate the fast signal. Can you confirm you’re satisfied with the stabilization and whether you want the credit proposal started now? I’ll coordinate next steps with Marcus and our finance team.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference, inc.

— Marcus Lin (added inline): I support the 25% credit recommendation given outage impact; I’ll draft the formal credit memo and start approvals with finance today.
